To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amount and size of the Pd nanoparticles deposited electrochemically on pyridine- terminated SAMs can be controlled by adjusting the sample potentials during complexation and deposition.
the potential of the sample during the complexation of the Pd(2+)-ions with the pyridine-nitrogens of the SAM is crucial for the amount of PPD and thus for the size of the Pd nanoparticles.
the potential of the substrate during the complexation between the pyridine nitroge...n atoms of the thiol SAM and the palladium cations plays a crucial role in the metallization process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrochemical metallization of organic films.
the complexation kinetics between Pd cations in solution and the pyridine nitro- gen atoms on top of the araliphatic thiols, and its influence on the metallization of organic films.
the complexation kinetics of pyridine ligands for metallization of self-assembled monolyayers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kinetics of the metal complexation step is a key parameter for the control of the morphology of metal nanostructures on SAMs.
the electrostatic potential of the SAM surface plays a decisive role in the metallization process.
the kinetics of the metallization of organic films is governed by the electrostatic interaction between the metal cations and the pyridyl nitrogens, which is controlled by the sample potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the kinetics of the Pd(2+)/(pyridine)-thiol complexation is strongly dependent on the surface charge and the amount of Pdm+ ions coordinated on the surface.
the electrochemical complexation between Pd(2+)-ions and pyridyl groups of the SAM is the key step for the metallization process.
the electrochemical metallization of organic films is a complex multistep process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by adjusting the sample bias during the complexation process the amount of PAd(II) ions coordinated to the SAM can be controlled, which in turn allows for the control over the particle size.
the complexation kinetics can be used to tune the size of the Pd particles by adjusting the amount of coordinated Pd ions.
the kinetics of the Pd complexation can be adjusted by tuning the sample potential, which in turn allows the control of the size of the nanoparticles.
